title: ALMA Detection of Extended [C II] Emission in Himiko at z = 6.6
question: Is [CII] 158um emission detected in the Lya emitter Himiko at z=6.595 when Cycle 0 and Cycle 1 ALMA data are combined, how does it compare with the local L[CII]-SFR relation, and how does it relate to the UV clumps?

data.sensitivity: Combined continuum 9 uJy/beam; line 88 uJy per 100 km/s channel

evidence.quote: our detection places Himiko along the local L$_{\rm[CII]}$-SFR given by (cite: De-Looze:2014)

what.value: HST UV clump photometry and Lya data / SED metallicity

evidence.quote: Clumps A and B are separated by a projected distance of 6.4 kpc, while the other two clumps have a separation of 2.5 kpc (cite: Zabl:2015).
placing an upper limit for the [Cii] luminosity at L$_{\rm[CII]}$$<5.4\times10^{7}$ L$_{\odot}$

recipe.method: Standard ALMA scripts, then CASA clean with natural weighting for continuum and 5 km/s cubes
Joint imaging of both programs, plus uv-tapered cube to recover extended emission
Moment map over 270 km/s centred at -185 km/s; spectrum extracted within the 2 sigma contours, rebinned to 40 km/s
Channel-map analysis of the non-smoothed combined cube; 2D elliptical Gaussian fit to channel map
3 sigma limit converted to L_IR with grey-body, then to SFR_IR

evidence.quote: The line is offset by $-145\pm15$ km/s relative to the $z_{\rm Ly\alpha}$
has a line width of $130\pm30$ km/s

not_stated_but_needed: clean masks, threshold, iterations, cell and image size
Which Cycle 0 calibration/flagging beyond standard scripts
How the total flux and 9 sigma significance were computed
Procedure for the Gaussian fits and size deconvolution
SFR_UV conversion and the metallicity-relation details
Method for the 100 km/s upper limits
score_reason: Public data and a simple recipe, but many imaging and extraction details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a simple recipe and numeric results (flux, L[CII], offset).
